results.location: 2 Controlling the adversarial robustness of a neural network through the singular spectrum of its layers
results.content: The adversarial robustness of a neural network f ... can be measured by its relative sensitivity S to small perturbations δ, i.e., S(f, X, δ) := (‖f(X+δ) − f(X)‖/‖f(X)‖)(‖X‖/‖δ‖). ... S can be bounded [35] by the product S(f, X, δ) ≤ (∏_{ℓ=1}^L κ(W^ℓ)) (∏_{ℓ=1}^L κ(σ^ℓ)) (1) where κ(W) := ‖W‖‖W^†‖ is the condition number of a matrix W, W^† is the pseudo-inverse of W, and κ(σ) is the condition number of the layer activation function σ.
results.route_rationale: Eq (1) is a bound cited to [35] that rests on neural-network composition machinery and on an activation condition number κ(σ) the paper never defines; not a crisp self-contained formal claim.

results.location: 2 Controlling the adversarial robustness of a neural network through the singular spectrum of its layers
results.content: The sensitivity of a low-rank factorized network can be readily deduced from Equation (1) by leveraging orthonormality of U and V, i.e., κ(USV^⊤) = κ(S).
results.route_rationale: Closed-form unitary-invariance identity for the condition number; a real linear-algebra argument, machine-checkable.

lean_result.reasoning: Formalised κ(USVᵀ) = κ(S) with κ(A) = ‖A‖·‖A⁻¹‖ in the Frobenius norm, for U,V orthogonal (UᵀU = 1, VᵀV = 1). Proved ‖U·S·Vᵀ‖ = ‖S‖ (via the trace identity (U·S·Vᵀ)ᵀ(U·S·Vᵀ) = V·SᵀS·Vᵀ and cyclic trace), (U·S·Vᵀ)⁻¹ = V·S⁻¹·Uᵀ, and ‖(U·S·Vᵀ)⁻¹‖ = ‖S⁻¹‖. The theorem cond_mul_orthogonal_left_right compiles cleanly with only the standard Mathlib axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). Note: the paper's κ uses the spectral norm; the identity holds for any unitarily invariant norm, and the paper itself works with the Frobenius norm for the regularizer, so the formalisation is faithful to the mathematical content.

lean.formal_statement: theorem cond_mul_orthogonal_left_right {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (U S V : Matrix n n ℝ) (hU : Uᵀ * U = 1) (hV : Vᵀ * V = 1) : cond (U * S * Vᵀ) = cond S

results.content: Definition 1. We define the robustness regularizer R for any S ∈ R^{r×r} by R(S) = ||S^T S − α_S^2 I||, where α_S^2 = (1/r) ||S||^2. (2) and I = I_r is the r × r identity matrix. ... Here α_S is chosen such that ||S|| = ||α_S I||.
results.route_rationale: Definitional; the stated property ‖S‖ = ‖α_S I‖ is an elementary norm identity checkable by inspection.

results.content: Moreover, R is also a scaled standard deviation of the squared singular values {σ_i(S)^2}_{i=1}^r, i.e., (1/r) R(S)^2 = (1/r) ∑_{i=1}^r (σ_i(S)^2)^2 − ( (1/r) ∑_{i=1}^r σ_i(S)^2 )^2. (3)
results.route_rationale: Closed-form identity connecting the regularizer to the variance of squared singular values; correctness turns on the derivation.

lean_result.reasoning: Formalised the algebraic content of Eq (3)/(26): for any square matrix S, ‖SᵀS − (‖S‖²/r)·I‖² = ‖SᵀS‖² − ‖S‖⁴/r in the Frobenius norm (theorem regularizer_sq_identity, with ‖·‖² = trace(·ᵀ·) and r = card n). The variance form of Eq (3) follows additionally from σ_i(SᵀS) = σ_i(S)², which turns ‖SᵀS‖² = Σ σ_i(S)⁴ and ‖S‖⁴ = (Σ σ_i(S)²)². Compiles cleanly; axioms are only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

lean.formal_statement: theorem regularizer_sq_identity {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] (S : Matrix n n ℝ) : frobSq (Sᵀ * S - (frobSq S / (Fintype.card n : ℝ)) • 1) = frobSq (Sᵀ * S) - (frobSq S)^2 / (Fintype.card n : ℝ)

results.content: Therefore, R is a unitarily invariant regularizer; namely, R(USV^T) = R(S) for orthogonal U, V.
results.route_rationale: Unitary-invariance claim for the regularizer; follows from a real linear-algebra argument, machine-checkable.

lean_result.reasoning: Formalised reg(USVᵀ) = reg(S) with reg(X) = ‖XᵀX − (‖X‖²/r)·I‖ (Frobenius) for orthogonal U,V (theorem reg_mul_orthogonal_left_right). The proof uses (USVᵀ)ᵀ(USVᵀ) = V·(SᵀS)·Vᵀ (UᵀU = 1 collapses the U-factors) and the V-congruence invariance ‖V·M·Vᵀ − c·I‖ = ‖M − c·I‖ (trace-cyclic + VᵀV = 1). Compiles cleanly; axioms are only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

lean.formal_statement: theorem reg_mul_orthogonal_left_right {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] (U S V : Matrix n n ℝ) (hU : Uᵀ * U = 1) (hV : Vᵀ * V = 1) : reg (U * S * Vᵀ) = reg S

results.content: Proposition 1. The gradient of R in (2) is given by ∇R(S) = 2 S (S^T S − α_S^2 I) / R(S).
results.route_rationale: Formalisable calculus identity for the gradient; correctness turns on a real Fréchet-derivative argument.

lean_result.reasoning: Attempted a faithful formalisation of the load-bearing directional-derivative identity for Q = R²: HasDerivAt (fun t => Q (S + t·Z)) (4·⟨S·(SᵀS − α_S²·I), Z⟩) 0, from which ∇R = 2S(SᵀS−α²I)/R follows by the chain rule. The statement elaborates and the derivative machinery (product rule, polynomial derivative at 0) works, but the load-bearing polynomial expansion of Q(S + tZ) (the t-linear coefficient computation) could not be completed within budget, leaving a sorry (sorryAx). A faithful statement of the full Fréchet derivative of R itself also requires a NormedSpace structure on Matrix n n ℝ that the shared project does not provide. A FAILED Lean run is not evidence about the claim either way.

lean.formal_statement: theorem gradient_Q_directional {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] (S Z : Matrix n n ℝ) : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => Q (S + t • Z)) (4 * finner (S * (Sᵀ * S - alphaSq S • 1)) Z) 0

fallback_result.reasoning: Informal review of the claim Lean could not settle (the Fréchet gradient of R). The appendix proof (Eqs 27–30) is correct: with Q = R² and W_S = SᵀS − α_S²I, one computes (1/2)∇Q(S)[Z] = (W_S, ZᵀS + SᵀZ − (2/r)(S,Z)I); using (W_S, I) = ‖S‖² − α_S²‖I‖² = 0 (since α_S² = ‖S‖²/r and ‖I‖² = r) and the cyclic inner-product identities (W_S, ZᵀS) = (S·W_S, Z) = (W_S, SᵀZ), one gets ∇Q(S) = 4S(SᵀS − α_S²I), hence ∇R(S) = ∇Q/(2R) = 2S(SᵀS − α_S²I)/R(S). Verified correct.

results.content: Proposition 2 (Condition number bound). For any S ∈ R^{r×r} there holds κ(S) ≤ exp( (1 / (2 σ_r(S))) R(S) ) + c, where c is a constant that may depend on r and the spectrum structure. Due to variations in σ_r(S) during training, the bound may not reliably predict the condition number throughout. Thus, R(S) provides a heuristic rather than a strict quantitative control on the conditioning.
results.route_rationale: The main-text statement carries an unspecified, spectrum-dependent constant c (making it vacuous as written) and does not match the appendix's proven bound; best judged informally against the appendix derivation.
The appendix's clean condition-number bound; a real inequality chain (variance-to-range + MVT-for-log), machine-checkable.

lean_result.reasoning: Formalised the abstract inequality chain (33)+(34)+(35): for extreme singular values 0 < σᵣ ≤ σ₁ and regularizer value R ≥ 0 satisfying R² ≥ (σ₁² − σᵣ²)²/2 (the variance/range inequality (32)), one has ln(σ₁/σᵣ) ≤ R/(√2·σᵣ²) (theorem condition_number_log_bound). The two load-bearing lemmas — the MVT-for-log bound ln(σ₁/σᵣ) ≤ (σ₁²−σᵣ²)/(2σᵣ²) (via log(x) ≤ x−1 and σᵣ ≤ σ₁) and the range-to-regularizer step √2·R ≥ σ₁²−σᵣ² (via (√2R)² = 2R² ≥ (σ₁²−σᵣ²)²) — are machine-checked. The formalisation abstracts over σ₁, σᵣ, R; the connection to the matrix S is the standard singular-value interpretation. Note this bound, κ ≤ exp(R/(√2·σᵣ²)), is exactly what the appendix proves and differs from the main-text Proposition 2 statement. Compiles cleanly; axioms only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

lean.formal_statement: theorem condition_number_log_bound {σ₁ σᵣ R : ℝ} (hpos : 0 < σᵣ) (hle : σᵣ ≤ σ₁) (hR : 0 ≤ R) (hvar : R ^ 2 ≥ (σ₁ ^ 2 - σᵣ ^ 2) ^ 2 / 2) : Real.log (σ₁ / σᵣ) ≤ R / (Real.sqrt 2 * σᵣ ^ 2)

results.content: Proposition 3. Consider the dynamical system generated by the gradient flow of J; namely, Ṡ(t) + β∇R(S(t)) + S(t) = M. Then for any t > 0 we have the long-time stability estimate 1/2 ||S(t) − M||² + 2β ∫₀ᵗ e^{τ−t} R(S(τ)) dτ ≤ 1/2 e^{−t} ||S(0) − M||² + 2(1 − e^{−t}) β(1 + 2β) ||M||². (5)
results.route_rationale: Long-time stability estimate; a differential-inequality + Grönwall bound, formalisable in principle.

lean_result.reasoning: Attempted a faithful formalisation of the abstract Grönwall-with-forcing core (the step (41)→(42) of the appendix): from u' + u + 4βR ≤ 2C on [0,t] with R ≥ 0, derive u(t) + 4β∫₀ᵗ e^{τ−t}R(τ)dτ ≤ u(0)e^{−t} + 2C(1−e^{−t}) (theorem gronwall_with_forcing). The statement elaborates and the integrating-factor setup (w = u·eˣ and its derivative (u'+u)·eˣ) was proven, but completing the proof requires extensive integrability/FTC plumbing (IntervalIntegrable hypotheses, integral monotonicity, module-instance resolution) that exceeded the budget, leaving sorries (sorryAx). A fully faithful statement of the paper's claim additionally requires a matrix-valued gradient-flow ODE over a Frobenius-normed space, and the shared project has no Norm instance on Matrix n n ℝ. A FAILED Lean run is not evidence about the claim either way.

lean.formal_statement: theorem gronwall_with_forcing {u u' R : ℝ → ℝ} {t C β : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) (hder : ∀ x ∈ Set.uIcc 0 t, HasDerivAt u (u' x) x) (hineq : ∀ x ∈ Set.uIcc 0 t, u' x + u x + 4 * β * R x ≤ 2 * C) (hR : ∀ x ∈ Set.uIcc 0 t, 0 ≤ R x) (huint : IntervalIntegrable u' MeasureTheory.volume 0 t) (hRint : IntervalIntegrable R MeasureTheory.volume 0 t) : u t + 4 * β * ∫ x in 0..t, Real.exp (x - t) * R x ≤ u 0 * Real.exp (-t) + 2 * C * (1 - Real.exp (-t))

fallback_result.reasoning: Informal review of the claim Lean could not settle (the long-time stability estimate). The appendix proof (Eqs 36–42) is verified step-by-step and is correct: (36) rewriting the flow as (d/dt)(S−M) + β∇R + (S−M) = 0; (37) testing against S−M gives (1/2)(d/dt)‖S−M‖² + β(∇R,S) + ‖S−M‖² = β(∇R,M); (38) ⟨S(SᵀS−α²I),S⟩ = ‖SᵀS‖² − (1/r)‖S‖⁴ = R(S)²; (39) (∇R,S) = 2R(S); (40) β(∇R,M) ≤ (1/2)‖S−M‖² + 2β(1+2β)‖M‖² — valid (the constant 2β(1+2β) is looser than the Young-optimal 2β(1+β) but still a correct bound, since (a−2βb)² ≥ 0); (41) the differential inequality; (42) Grönwall's inequality applied to u' + u ≤ 2C − 4βR yields exactly the stated integral bound. Verified correct.

results.content: Proof of (3). We calculate R(S)^2 = (S^T S − α_S^2 I, S^T S − α_S^2 I) = ‖S^T S‖^2 − 2α_S^2(S^T S, I) + α_S^4(I, I) = ‖S^T S‖^2 − (1/r)‖S‖^4 = ∑_{i=1}^r σ_i(S^T S)^2 − (1/r)(∑_{i=1}^r σ_i(S)^2)^2 (26) = r( (1/r)∑_{i=1}^r σ_i(S^T S)^2 − ((1/r)∑_{i=1}^r σ_i(S)^2)^2 ). Since S^T S is symmetric positive semidefinite, σ_i(S^T S) = σ_i(S)^2. Applying this substitution yields (3).
results.route_rationale: Informal review of the derivation establishing Eq (3); supplements the Lean check of the algebraic core (26).

results.content: Proof of Proposition 1. ... (1/2) ∇Q(S)[Z] = (W_S, Z^⊤S + S^⊤Z − (2/r)(S, Z) I) = (S W_S^⊤, Z) + (S W_S, Z) − (2/r)(S, Z)(W_S, I) (27) = 2 (S (S^⊤S − α_S^2 I), Z) − (2/r)(S, Z)(S^⊤S − α_S^2 I, I). Note by definition of α_S^2, (S^⊤S − α_S^2 I, I) = ‖S‖^2 − α_S^2 ‖I‖^2 = 0. (28) Hence ∇Q(S) = 4 S (S^⊤S − α_S^2 I). (29) Since R^2 = Q, therefore ∇R(S) = ∇Q(S) / (2 R(S)). (30)

results.content: Proof of Proposition 2. From (26) there holds (1/r) R(S)^2 = (1/r) ∑_{i=1}^r σ_i(S^⊤S)^2 − ((1/r) ∑_{i=1}^r σ_i(S^⊤S))^2. (31) ... (1/r) 𝓡(S)^2 ≥ (ϛ_1(S^⊤S) − ϛ_r(S^⊤S))^2/(2r) = (ϛ_1(S)^2 − ϛ_r(S)^2)^2/(2r). (32) Hence √2 𝓡(S) ≥ ϛ_1(S)^2 − ϛ_r(S)^2. (33) ... ln(κ(S)) ≤ (ϛ_1(S)^2 − ϛ_r(S)^2)/(2ϛ_r(S)^2). (34) Combining (33) and (34) yields ln(κ(S)) ≤ (1/(√2 ϛ_r(S)^2)) 𝓡(S). (35) which, after exponentiation, yields (4).

(37) ... ⟨S(S^⊤S − α_S^2 I), S⟩ = ‖S^⊤S‖^2 − (1/r)‖S‖^4 = 𝓡(S)^2. (38) Hence (∇𝓡(S), S) = 2𝓡(S). findings.evidence: The main-text Proposition 2 claims κ(S) ≤ exp(R(S)/(2σ_r(S))) + c, where c 'may depend on r and the spectrum structure'. As written this is vacuous — c may absorb any per-S deficit — so no quantitative bound is actually stated. It also does not match the paper's own appendix derivation (Proof of Prop 2, Eqs 31–35), which proves the different bound κ(S) ≤ exp(R(S)/(√2·σ_r(S)²)): the exponent differs in both the power of σ_r and the constant, and R/σ_r is not scale-invariant (R scales like ‖S‖², σ_r like ‖S‖). The valid, non-vacuous bound lives in the appendix; the headline statement is misstated.
findings.exact_quote: Proposition 2 (Condition number bound). For any S ∈ R^{r×r} there holds κ(S) ≤ exp( (1 / (2 σ_r(S))) R(S) ) + c, where c is a constant that may depend on r and the spectrum structure.

summary: Mathematical verification of 'Dynamical Low-Rank Compression of Neural Networks with Robustness under Adversarial Attacks' (Schotthöfer, Yang, Schnake). 14 self-contained snippets were extracted (7 routed to informal verify-math, 7 to a shared Lean 4 project under MATH_VERIFICATION/Paper) and every snippet was checked. Lean machine-checked 5 of the paper's core identities: the unitary invariance of the condition number κ(USVᵀ)=κ(S), the regularizer identity ‖SᵀS−(‖S‖²/r)I‖²=‖SᵀS‖²−‖S‖⁴/r (the algebraic content of Eq 3), the unitary invariance of the regularizer R(USVᵀ)=R(S), the appendix's condition-number bound ln κ ≤ R/(√2·σ_r²) (Eq 35), and the conv/Tucker index rearrangement (Eqs 10→11). The two remaining Lean targets — the gradient formula ∇R = 2S(SᵀS−α²I)/R (Prop 1) and the long-time stability estimate (Prop 3/Eq 5) — could not be settled by Lean within budget (the polynomial-expansion and Grönwall/integrability steps respectively; both also require a Frobenius-normed matrix ODE infrastructure the project lacks); both were reviewed informally as fallbacks and found correct step-by-step (their appendix proofs are valid, including the loose-but-correct constant 2β(1+2β) in Eq 40). One finding: the main-text Proposition 2 statement κ(S) ≤ exp(R/(2σ_r))+c is vacuous as written (c may depend on the spectrum) and inconsistent with the appendix's own derivation, which proves κ(S) ≤ exp(R/(√2·σ_r²)); the two verifiers do not disagree on any single claim — the Lean PASSED appendix bound (Eq 35) and the informal review confirm the same mathematics, and the finding concerns the main-text statement's mismatch with its own proof. The shared Lean project MATH_VERIFICATION/Paper was reused (it pre-existed this run) and is kept on disk.
